hypotheses.cause: Strongest hypothesis: the V100 (g1.x) and A100 (g2.x) hardware was lost in the October 2026 drone strikes, and DataSphere has nowhere to put a g1/g2 VM. Before 21 Oct 2026, Yandex's own docs said V100 (gpu-standard-v1 Broadwell and gpu-standard-v2 Cascade Lake) and A100 (gpu-standard-v3) VMs could only be created in ru-central1-a and ru-central1-b. Those zones are the Vladimir and Sasovo data centres. Sasovo stopped on 8 Oct, and zone b was not restored as of the last reports found. Vladimir stopped on 11 Oct. Since 23 Oct ru-central1-a is a 'new location' that keeps the old name and has limited capacity. T4/T4i (gt4.1, gt4i.1) were also supported in ru-central1-d, which survived. So the scheduler finds no g1/g2 host, returns 'Unable to allocate any VM' and falls back to T4.
hypotheses.evidence: (1) The Russian GPU docs include, before it was deleted, said: 'Виртуальные машины на платформах {{ v100-broadwell }}, {{ v100-cascade-lake }} и {{ a100-epyc }} можно создать в зонах доступности {{ region-id }}-a и {{ region-id }}-b'. The English include still says the same today. (2) Before the incident, the VM platforms 'Ограничения' table marked V100 Broadwell, V100 Cascade Lake and A100 as NOT supported in ru-central1-d or ru-central1-e. T4 and T4i were supported in ru-central1-d; I confirmed this by decoding the yes/no SVG icons. (3) Release 21.10.2026 (commit ee1c155e70) deleted gpu-zones.md and the whole restrictions table. It also deleted the list of zones from geo-scope.md, and the 'a and b' wording from the DataSphere release notes and node docs. The V100 and A100 platform rows stay in vm-platforms.md as of the 5 Nov release. (4) In the DataSphere docs, g1.x = Intel Broadwell + V100 (that is, gpu-standard-v1), g2.x = AMD EPYC + A100, and gt4.1 = Ice Lake + T4. (5) Official alerts channel: 8 Oct, ru-central1-b lost power, and 'возобновить работу зоны в ближайшее время не удастся'. 11 Oct, the Vladimir data centre 'полностью остановлена', 'Оставшуюся конфигурацию ресурсов считаем неустойчивой', and the platform is in emergency mode. (7) The status page snapshot taken 2026-11-09 19:48 UTC still has features.emergencyMode=true. Its banner sends users to Cloud Center for current status, and its incidents API returns 'API is not available at this moment'. (8) The DataSphere docs say a community is created in one zone, all its projects and resources live in that zone, and it cannot be moved.

hypotheses.fits_facts: It explains all the key facts. g1.1 fails every time, across more than 33 hours (2026-11-08 07:56 to 2026-11-09 17:35 UTC), with an allocation error rather than an access error. In the mixed list, both g1.1 and g2.1 were skipped, and both are V100/A100 platforms that existed only in zones a/b. gt4.1 (T4) allocated seven VMs at once, which fits because T4 was supported in the surviving ru-central1-d and evidently exists wherever this community's VMs now run. c1.4 runs normally. The roughly 3-minute fallback in the mixed config fits two sequential ~90-second attempts (g1.1, then g2.1) before gt4.1; this timing match is my inference. The project Configurations page still listing g1/g2 as enabled fits too: that page shows entitlements and prices, not live capacity, and the DataSphere configuration docs have not changed since 13 Jul 2026.

I do not know which zone community bt1t5m46lhju7eabr0qh was created in, or whether any gpu-standard-v1/v3 hosts were reinstalled after the incident. The supercomputers' A100s were reportedly moved to new sites (ru-bezh.ru, 28 Oct; aif.ru), but those are Yandex's internal ML clusters, not cloud capacity. (1) The owner, not the service account, which gets 403, reads the community's zoneId through the console or GET https://datasphere.api.cloud.yandex.net/datasphere/v2/communities/bt1t5m46lhju7eabr0qh; the field is documented in ru/datasphere/api-ref/Community/get.md, lines 54 and 88-90. (2) The owner files a support ticket with the community ID, the project ID, the failed g1.1 job IDs and operation IDs with their UTC times, and the question: 'Are there any gpu-standard-v1/v3 (g1.x/g2.x) hosts available for DataSphere in this community's zone after the October incident?' If both end in ERROR 'Unable to allocate any VM' after about 90 seconds while [gt4.1] allocates within minutes, that matches this hypothesis. hypotheses.fix_where: This cannot be fixed in our code or job configs. It is Yandex-side capacity. Workarounds: keep jobs on gt4.1 (T4, 16 GB) or gt4i.1 (T4i, 24 GB) and size the work to fit; or ask support whether g1/g2 exists in some zone and whether a new community there would get it (communities cannot be moved between zones, per resource-model.md line 7); or use another provider, which Yandex itself recommended (Selectel, K2Cloud, VK Cloud per https://t.me/yandexcloudalerts/1520), or the local RTX 5090.

hypotheses.cause: Second possibility: emergency capacity and quota rationing after the incident throttles GPU allocation even where some hardware may exist. Since 10 Oct, Compute quotas are managed manually. Extra quotas were suspended on 11 Oct. The new ru-central1-a opened with explicitly limited capacity that Yandex expands step by step, giving priority to critical restorations. ruled_out: A billing gate (top-up, paid consumption, ≥500 ₽). gt4.1 and gt4i.1 carry the same footnote 1 and are allocated. The documented gating error is 'Access Denied: Spec gX.X is not available for your cloud' (ru/datasphere/qa/index.md #gpu-access), not 'Unable to allocate any VM'. g1.1 and g1.2 have no footnote at all. Topping up the billing account does nothing here.
The project unit balance or limits. The owner removed them, the API shows empty Limits and an empty unitBalance, and the failures continued exactly as before.
'Maximum number of VMs in the project' (MAX_VM_COUNT_PER_PROJECT, now 20). g1.1 failed while the project had 0 or 1 other jobs running, and raising it changed nothing.
A per-spec quota as the common cause. g1.1 and g1.2 have no quota row in ru/_includes/datasphere-limits.md, yet they fail in exactly the same way as g2.x.
The job YAML or the CLI. JobParameters has no zone, platform or reservation field, the instance names are passed through unchanged, and the same CLI and config succeed with gt4.1.
A service-account-wide GPU ban. The same service account gets gt4.1 (7 at once) and gt4i.1.
ru-central1-e as the community's zone. The Compute restrictions table marks T4/T4i 'no' in zone e, but T4 works here.
Planned V100 end-of-life on its own. There is no deprecation notice, and it would not explain A100 (g2.1/g2.2) failing too.
The 'Configurations' page as evidence of availability. It shows permissions and prices, not physical capacity in the zone, and since 19:46 UTC on 11-09 the server has even rejected g1.1 at creation.

'Job execution quota exhausted' as a cause of the V100 failures. It is a separate, real issue: instant RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on gt4.1 jobs at 12:22:28 and 12:47:54 UTC on 11-08 with 0 active jobs in this project, and at 17:46-17:58 UTC on 11-09 with 8 active. It is not controlled by the Restrictions tab, and its scope and value are undocumented (limits page: 'Количество активных заданий 10').
H1.1's claim that cloud_quota_audit.json L47/L59 shows ALLOW_SPEC_G_1_1/G_2_1 'enabled'. That file contains only restrictionsMeta (names and value types), not values, so the source does not say this.
